`UnifiedActivationPipeline` (`.aios-core/development/scripts/unified-activation-pipeline.js`) is the single entry point for all 12 agents. `generate-greeting.js` delegates to `UnifiedActivationPipeline.activate(agentId)`. Pipeline phases: 1) 5 parallel loaders (`Promise.all`); 2) agent def; 3) sequential preference/session type/workflow; 4) enriched context; 5) `GreetingBuilder`. `loadUserProfile()` runs in `buildGreeting()` and is passed to `_buildContextualGreeting()` to avoid duplicate `resolveConfig()` calls. `GreetingPreferenceManager.getPreference(userProfile)` accepts optional profile for bob restriction; PM bypasses restriction. Bob non-PM: `auto` shows redirect; forced `named` shows simple named greeting; commands empty. `_safeGetPermissionBadge()` supplies badge.

8 agents have command `visibility: [full, quick, key]`; `qa`, `data-engineer`, `devops`, `ux-design-expert` lack metadata and fall back to first 12 commands. `aios-master` uses `visibility: full`. `*yolo` is universal. Formats: structured (`name: xxx`) vs compact (`key: 'value'`); compact agents: qa, devops, data-engineer, ux-design-expert. Always match existing format when editing. Source `.aios-core/development/agents/`; Claude mirror `.claude/commands/AIOS/agents/`; separate files, synced separately by `ideSync`.

All greeting section builders (`buildPresentation`, `buildRoleDescription`, `buildProjectStatus`, `buildFooter`, `buildContextSection`) accept optional `sectionContext`; `_buildContextualGreeting` builds it from enriched context and passes it to all builders. With context, presentation uses brief named greeting for existing/workflow sessions; without it, archetypal greeting (backward compatible). `_formatProjectStatusNarrative()` makes natural language; without context, legacy `_formatProjectStatus()` remains. `_safeBuildSection(fn)` wraps builders with SECTION_TIMEOUT (150ms) and try/catch. `Promise.all([contextSection, workflowSection])` parallelizes sections. Footer: new=`*guide`; existing=`*help + *session-info`; workflow=`Focused on **{story}**`. ACT-5 changes (lines 661-816 in greeting-builder.js) must NOT be touched -- they own workflow navigator section.

`resolveConfig()` merges L1-L5; L5 (`user-config.yaml`) highest priority. `user_profile` is USER_FIELD in `migrate-config.js`; `toggleUserProfile()` in `config-resolver.js` flips bob<->advanced. `validateUserProfile()` in `validate-user-profile.js` is pure; no filesystem/mock needed. Always mock `fs`, `js-yaml`, `config-resolver`, and dependency modules BEFORE requiring the module under test. For repeated `resolveConfig`, use `mockReturnValue`, not `mockReturnValueOnce`. Double `loadUserProfile()` caused failures with `mockReturnValueOnce`.

`PermissionMode` and `OperationGuard` in `.aios-core/core/permissions/` work; `cycleMode()` and `enforcePermission()` wired in `index.js`. Cycle: `explore`(0)->`ask`(1)->`auto`(2), `PermissionMode.MODE_CYCLE`.

Locks: Use `fs.writeFile(path, data, { flag: 'wx' })` for exclusive create lock; include PID+timestamp; stale threshold ~10s, timeout ~3s, poll 50ms. Temp `{path}.tmp.{pid}` + `fs.rename()`; Windows rename fails if target exists, fall back to direct `fs.writeFile()`. Cache fingerprint: `.git/HEAD` mtime + `.git/index` mtime. Worktree-aware path: `git rev-parse --git-dir`; detect worktree/main tree: `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`. For writeFile dual lock/cache mocks, use broad `mockResolvedValue` and filter `mock.calls`. Mock `child_process.execSync` separately from `execa`. Use `jest.requireActual('fs')` for real hook-existence checks.
